correctness.rationale: In normalized Haar measure the exact Toeplitz moments are 2 sin(ka) cos(k beta)/(pi k), with diagonal 2a/pi. At antipodal placement the odd and even character blocks have sizes two and three. The smaller eigenvalue of the symmetric two-dimensional piece of the even block lies strictly below all other eigenvalues, since h=(sqrt(p^2+8)-p)/2>1 and |p|<1. Reconstructed the shifted trial form on 1 and the cosine quadratic, independently dropping the constant term of the latter. Dividing the determinant by the positive common scale and reducing modulo y^2+c(2c^2-1)y-2c^2 gives t^2(A+t^2D), t=cos(beta). The bounding quadratics for h and the strict signs of A,D were checked by exact arithmetic, using the positive-coefficient transform c=x/(1+x) for the signs on 0<c<1. Every nonantipodal placement, including touching arcs at beta=a, has t>0 and a negative determinant, so its least Rayleigh quotient is strictly smaller. The exact Taylor series has leading term 64 a^5/(135 pi).
residual_risks: The proof does not cover unequal widths, arbitrary masks, widths at the empty/full endpoints, or more than five characters.

checked_sources: Frozen Fourier observation model and strict trial-form comparison; prior all-band asymptotic and exact lower-band results
value.rationale: At fixed observation measure, maximizing the worst captured energy is the sharp conditioning problem for continuous observation on two equal sensor arcs. The first nontrivial extension beyond the previously known three-mode exact case and the known small-arc leading law gives a usable finite-width benchmark: it identifies the placement uniquely and quantifies conditioning at every width, not just at an endpoint. The two-vector comparison proves a structural result that would not follow from diagonalizing only the antipodal case.
residual_risks: Equal widths are essential to the comparison; the broader unequal-width design can perform better and is not resolved at finite widths here.
